A scroll film, built with coding agents

The top of this site is one scroll-driven film. Five scenes share one GSAP timeline, shaders draw the fire and the red sky, and a static version takes over when motion is turned off.

The problem

A portfolio is a list of links until someone feels how you build. I wanted the first screen to be something I made with motion and graphics code, and I wanted it to stay fast, readable and usable for people who turn animation off.

I also build with coding agents in the loop. So the process matters as much as the page: I write the brief, the agent proposes and edits, I review each diff and I check the result in a real browser before it is committed.

How it works

  1. One timeline.Each scene file only adds tweens to a shared GSAP timeline. ScrollTrigger pins the hero and scrubs the playhead as you scroll.
  2. Shaders where they pay off.The vortex, the red sky and the burn are WebGL fragment shaders. Contexts wake 2 seconds before a scene and render at 0.7 scale on desktop and 0.5 on phones.
  3. Canvas for the rest.Crows are seeded particles, so they fly the same way every time, and in-between frames for the arm raise are warped by optical flow.
  4. A way out.With reduced motion on, a static layout replaces the film. The theme switch, the command palette and these project pages all work without it.
  5. Checked, not assumed.Changes are verified in a browser at desktop and phone sizes, in both themes.

Limits and next steps

  • The film is long. The same QA pass measured the hero pinned for about 15,000 px of scroll on desktop, so there is a skip link to the work.
  • The scores above are from one desktop run. I have not re-run them on a phone profile or after the latest hero changes.
  • Visual consistency of the character art across scenes is still being worked on.
  • GSAP and Three.js load from pinned CDN versions. There is no fallback host if the CDN is down.

Built with
